candidate.answerReason: Working backward forces the last share to be a multiple of 1925. Taking that share to be 1925 makes every intermediate remainder integral and every share positive.

methods.label: Work backward from the final share
methods.explanation:
Working backward makes the remaining fractions especially simple. Let \(m\) be the positive integer number of coins received by the twelfth pirate. This is also the amount remaining just before that pirate takes a share.

The eleventh pirate leaves \(1/12\) of the previous remainder, so there were \(12m\) coins before that pirate's turn. The tenth pirate leaves \(2/12\), so the amount before that turn was \((12/2)(12m)\). Continuing backward, let \(R_j\) be the amount obtained after undoing \(j\) turns, where \(R_0=m\). Then
\[
R_j=\frac{m\,12^j}{j!},\qquad 0\le j\le11,
\]
where \(j!=1\cdot2\cdots j\) and \(0!=1\). In particular, the initial amount is
\[
N=R_{11}=\frac{m\,12^{11}}{11!}.
\]
Factoring the finite product \(11!\) gives
\[
11!=2^8\cdot3^4\cdot5^2\cdot7\cdot11
=12^4\cdot1925.
\]
Hence
\[
N=\frac{m\,12^7}{1925}.
\]
Since \(1925=5^2\cdot7\cdot11\) has no prime factors in common with \(12\), integrality of \(N\) forces \(m\) to be a multiple of \(1925\). Also, \(N\) is a fixed positive multiple of \(m\), so minimizing \(N\) is equivalent to minimizing the feasible \(m\).

It remains to check that \(m=1925\) makes every turn work, not just the initial amount. For \(0\le j\le3\), the denominator \(j!\) divides \(12^j\), so \(R_j\) is an integer. For \(4\le j\le11\), use \(1925=11!/12^4\) to write
\[
R_j=\frac{11!}{j!}\,12^{j-4},
\]
which is also an integer. All these amounts are positive. Moreover,
\[
R_j=\frac{12}{j}R_{j-1}>R_{j-1}
\qquad(1\le j\le11).
\]
Thus, in forward order, each of the first eleven pirates receives a positive integer difference of consecutive remainders, and the last receives \(m\). This proves feasibility as well as minimality.

The twelfth pirate therefore receives \(\boxed{1925}\) coins, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

The method uses a backward recurrence and prime-factor divisibility, then verifies every intermediate amount. review.mathematicalCheck: Reversing j turns gives R_j=m·12^j/j!, so N=m·12⁷/1925. Coprimality forces 1925 to divide m. For m=1925, the displayed formulas make every remainder integral, and consecutive remainders have positive integer differences. Since N is proportional to m, this also proves minimality.
